uncited: It differs from its sibling [Radiance Meshes](4929-radiance-meshes.md) by being a purely geometric connectivity structure derived from point proximity rather than a radiative transfer approximation, and it serves as the foundational connectivity for the parent [Adaptive Delaunay Update](4923-adaptive-delaunay-update.md).
- Input: A set of points $S = \{\mathbf{p}_1, \dots, \mathbf{p}_n\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$ (or $\mathbb{R}^3$ for tetrahedralization, though the source specifies planar properties).
- Voronoi Cells: Implicitly defined by half-plane intersections.
Compute the Voronoi diagram $\text{Vor}(S)$ for the point set $S$.
- Vertices of the triangulation are the points in $S$.
Form triangles by connecting vertices that share pairwise edges in the dual graph.
- **Cocircular Points**: The definition assumes no four points are cocircular.
- **Limitations**: Sensitive to the distribution of points; clusters of points can lead to long, thin triangles if not constrained.
The Delaunay triangulation is named after Boris Delaunay.
It is the straight-line dual of the Voronoi diagram.
